figure: FIGURE 15.2, panel (a) 'Caching removes prefill work' — y-axis
issue: The y-axis is labelled "Prefill FLOPs / req (GFLOP)" with the no-cache series drawn flat at 100, but the caption describes the same quantity as "a percent of no-cache prefill work". The axis unit and the caption unit are different quantities, and the absolute reading (100 GFLOP per request of prefill) contradicts the book's own canonical arithmetic by roughly five orders of magnitude.
evidence: The book's canonical prefill cost at 70B and 9,200 prompt tokens is 2P/token × 9,200 = 1.4e11 × 9,200 = 1.29e15 FLOP ≈ 1.3 × 10⁶ GFLOP per request — not 100 GFLOP. The same page's prose (printed 227) uses 10¹⁴–10¹⁶ FLOP magnitudes for prefill. A reader who trusts the axis label will believe prefill costs ~100 GFLOP/request and will mis-scale every roofline or capacity calculation built on it; a reader who trusts the caption will read the axis as a percentage. The figure cannot be both.
acceptance_test: Choose one unit and make axis, caption, and any prose agree. Preferred: relabel the y-axis "Prefill FLOPs per request (% of no-cache)" with the no-cache series at 100, and state the absolute no-cache value in the caption (e.g. 'no-cache prefill ≈ 1.3 × 10¹⁵ FLOP at the canonical 70B/9,200-token prompt'). If the absolute GFLOP axis is retained instead, the plotted values must be rescaled to the canonical absolute figures and the caption must drop the 'percent' wording.

issue: Axis labels, tick labels, and the in-plot annotation are below the 8 pt print floor; at final trim size the rotated y-axis label and tick text may be difficult to read.
evidence: At 150 dpi, the rotated y-axis label 'Prefill FLOPs / req (% of no-cache)' and tick labels are roughly 10–12 px high (~5–6 pt), while the caption body is ~18 px (~8.6 pt). The right plot's y-axis label and tick labels are similarly small.
acceptance_test: Increase axis/tick/annotation label size to at least 8 pt at final trim size, or simplify and shorten labels and re-render; verify at 100% print size.

issue: The drawn 'with prefix cache' curve is concave-decreasing (roughly 100 → 96 → 92 → 88 → 83 → 76 → 65 at reuse 1, 2, 3, 5.6, 10.6, 30, 100), i.e. the saving per decade of reuse grows with reuse. That is the opposite of the amortization law the caption describes. If a prefix of P tokens is shared by r requests and each request also carries an uncached suffix S, per-request prefill falls from (S + P) to (S + P/r), so the ratio f(r) = (S + P/r)/(S + P) is convex-decreasing: the largest saving occurs between r = 1 and r = 10 and the curve then flattens toward S/(S + P).
evidence: Fitting the drawn curve to f(r) is impossible for any S/P: the drawn curve drops 15 points over r = 1→10 but a further 18 points over r = 10→100, whereas f(r) drops monotonically less per decade. For example, with S = 1.475P (which fits the drawn endpoint of 65 at r = 100), f(10) = 64 — the drawn value at r ≈ 10 is ≈ 83. The figure therefore teaches 'prefix caching's per-request saving accelerates with reuse', which is a false model of the mechanism and would mislead a reader sizing prefill headroom.
acceptance_test: Re-plot panel (a) from the stated model: choose and print a prefix/suffix split (e.g. P = 40% of the prompt), plot f(r) = (S + P/r)/(S + P) on the log-r axis, and label the curve with that formula or its parameters. The curve must be monotone and convex-decreasing, with the r = 1 point equal to the no-cache series. If a synthetic curve is retained for illustration, it must still satisfy the amortization shape.

figure: FIGURE 15.2, panel (b) title 'Decode bottleneck unaffected by caching'
issue: The panel title asserts a claim the panel does not show. Panel (b) plots 'Relative decode goodput (a.u.)' against 'Decode batch size' with a single blue curve; there is no caching axis, no cached/uncached pair, and no reference to prefix caching anywhere in the panel. The title is therefore an assertion about the absence of an effect that the data cannot demonstrate. The caption's own framing ('They are not competing on the same axis') is the defensible statement; the panel title is not.
evidence: Rendered page: panel (b) contains one series, one x-axis (decode batch size), one y-axis (relative decode goodput), one red dashed marker at batch ≈ 10, and a red annotation. Nothing in the panel encodes caching, so the title's claim is untested by the figure.
acceptance_test: Retitle panel (b) to what the axes show, e.g. 'Decode goodput scales with batch size (caching-independent axis)', and move the 'unaffected by caching' statement into the caption where it can be argued rather than asserted. If the claim is to be shown, the panel must include a cached and an uncached series.

figure: FIGURE 15.2, panel (b), red annotation at the batch ≈ 10 marker
issue: The red annotation contains an uninterpretable parenthetical: "diminishing gains past ~10 (6 hard plateau); goodput still rises; tail latency keeps rising". '(6 hard plateau)' is not a phrase a reader can parse — it is either a stray glyph, a truncated word, or a mangled '≈6× hard plateau'. The annotation is the figure's only statement of the operating-point recommendation, so its garbling matters.
evidence: Rendered page, panel (b): the annotation is set in small red type over four lines; the second line reads 'past ~10 (6 hard' and the third 'plateau); goodput'. The surrounding prose on printed 229 ('batching raises decode goodput (right plot) until binding saturates') does not disambiguate it either.
acceptance_test: Replace the parenthetical with a parseable phrase (e.g. 'past ~10 (hard plateau)') or remove it, and confirm the annotation's wording against the drawn curve: the curve rises from ≈32 at batch 10 to ≈90 at batch 100, so 'diminishing gains' must be stated in the multiplicative sense the curve actually shows.

figure: Figure 15.2, panel (b) (Decode bottleneck unaffected by caching)
issue: The red in-plot annotation ('diminishing gains / past ~b16 (no hard / plateau: goodput / still rises; tail / latency keeps rising)') is a dense 6-line block set in the smallest type in the figure; at the 150 dpi render its cap height is visibly smaller than the axis tick labels and appears to fall below the 8 pt print floor for figure in-text annotations.
evidence: Visual comparison on the rendered page: the red annotation glyphs are smaller than the '0/20/40/60/80/100' y-axis numerals and the '1/10' x-axis numerals, which are at or above the floor; the annotation is the only multi-line in-plot text and the tightest set.
acceptance_test: Enlarge the annotation to ≥8 pt, or reduce it to a short in-plot label (e.g. 'knee ~b16') and move the 'no hard plateau / tail latency keeps rising' clarification into the caption. Re-render and confirm the in-plot text meets the 8 pt floor.

issue: The x-axis quantity 'Avg prefix reuse' is used as the independent variable of the left plot but is never defined in the caption or the surrounding prose. A reader cannot tell whether it means the mean number of requests sharing a given prefix, the mean fraction of prompt tokens served from cache, or the mean reuse count per cached token — yet the curve's shape (100% at x=1, falling to ~60% at the right) depends on that definition.
evidence: Axis label: 'Avg prefix reuse'. Caption: 'prefill work vs average prefix reuse, as a percent of no-cache prefill work' — no operational definition given. Prose below the figure ('Goodput vs. Batch Size: the Cache Lever') also does not define it.
acceptance_test: Add a one-line definition to the caption, e.g. 'average prefix reuse = mean number of times a cached prefix block is reused across the request population (1 = no sharing, hence no prefill reduction)'. After the edit, the x=1 → 100% starting point must be self-evident from the definition.

issue: Wording tension between caption and in-plot annotation. The caption describes the right curve as 'rising until HBM bandwidth saturates', which a careful reader parses as an eventual flat plateau, while the in-plot annotation explicitly states 'no hard plateau: goodput still rises'. The intended meaning (asymptotic approach to the bandwidth ceiling, not a flat line in the shown range) is not stated in the caption.
evidence: Caption: 'batching raises decode goodput (right: decode goodput vs batch size, arbitrary goodput units, rising until HBM bandwidth saturates)'. In-plot red annotation: 'no hard plateau: goodput still rises; tail latency keeps rising'.
acceptance_test: Align the caption with the figure, e.g. 'rising, bending as it approaches the HBM-bandwidth ceiling (no hard plateau in the shown range)'. After the edit, the caption and the in-plot annotation must not be readable as 'eventually flat' vs 'never flat'.

page: PDF 273 / printed 253 (prose) vs PDF 278 / printed 258 (figure note)
issue: The prose that defines the figure's price band appears to give the $25/1K crossover as '10,856,693', but 155,816.93 / 0.025 = 6,232,677.2 and 155,816.93 / 0.015 = 10,387,795.3 (the printed low end reads 10,387,759.53, implying a numerator of 155,816.39 rather than 155,816.93). The figure's note and the prose's own '6.2–10.4M req/mo' region require the pair 6.23M / 10.39M, so the band edges drawn in FIGURE 16.1 are correct and the prose digits are the defect — but a reader who checks the prose against the figure will find them irreconcilable, and the figure's '6.2' end has no visible anchor.
evidence: Printed p. 253: 'the low end is 10,387,759.53 = 155,816.93 ÷ 0.015 (the $15/1K band) and the high end is 10,856,693 = 0.025 (the $25/1K band)'; figure note 'sensitivity = a $15–25/1K price band moves the break-even to 6.2–10.4M req/mo'.

figure: none (prose, §16.8 mini-case; no figure on this page)
issue: Two expressions of the same staff term in the end-of-chapter mini-case differ by ~10x: 0.5 FTE priced at '~$26K/mo' versus '~= $62K/yr fully loaded for one engineer'.
evidence: Quoted clause: 'the mini-case prices a startup's 0.5-FTE operator (~$26K/mo - ~= $62K/yr fully loaded for one engineer, a scenario value'. Re-derivation: 0.5 x $62K/yr = $31K/yr = $2.58K/mo, not $26K/mo. Inverse: $26K/mo x 12 / 0.5 = $624K/yr for one engineer. The $26K figure is load-bearing, not decorative: 'capex ~$11.6K + power ~$2.2K for two hosts leaves <= ~$26K for staff', and both '$40,000 / $0.0208 ~= 1.9M requests/month' and 'already ~2.6x past the break-even' depend on the $40K total (5M/1.923M = 2.60).
root_cause: One of the two parenthetical numbers carries a decimal-place error (or the FTE fraction does); the text equates them with an em-dash so the reader cannot tell which is authoritative.
correction: Reconcile to one internally consistent triple. Either restate the fully-loaded rate so 0.5 FTE x rate = $26K/mo, or correct the FTE fraction, or correct $26K/mo and recompute the $40K total, the 1.9M break-even and the ~2.6x headroom statement.
acceptance_test: 0.5 FTE x (stated fully-loaded annual rate) / 12 = the stated monthly staff term, AND $11.6K + $2.2K + staff term = the stated $40K all-in, AND $40,000 / $0.0208 and 5M / break-even both reproduce the printed results.

issue: The figure is over-annotated and several in-figure labels are below the 8 pt print floor at 8.5×11 trim size; the red break-even callout, green cloud callout, legend, and axis annotations require effort to read at 100% print size.
evidence: On the rendered 150 dpi page, the red box 'break-even ≈ 7.5M sensitivity ≈ 6.2–10.4M (a region, not a point)' and the green box 'cloud $87.6K/mo (occupancy input) priced at 6.24M req/mo only' have line heights of roughly 13–14 px, i.e. ~6.2–6.7 pt at 150 dpi; the legend and tick labels are similar. The figure also carries a top banner, title, four legend entries, four callout boxes, and three axis labels in one plot area.
acceptance_test: At 100% print size, every figure annotation measures at least 8 pt and remains legible without zoom; reduce callout text by moving derivation detail to the caption, enlarge remaining labels, and confirm no label is clipped or crowded.

issue: The x-axis label 'duration varied at FIXED 40 rps peak' does not distinguish peak-shaped-load duration from the canonical 624,000 s active window, so the canonical 6.24M marker can be misread as implying a 624,000 s peak duration rather than 156,000 s of peak load inside that window.

The prose on printed p. 254 says the canonical active window is 624,000 s (6.24M requests ÷ 10 rps) and that 'only how long the peak-shaped load runs inside the active window moves along x.' At 40 rps, the canonical 6.24M marker corresponds to 156,000 s of peak-shaped load, not 624,000 s; the figure's label does not say 'peak-shaped load duration'.
acceptance_test: Revise the x-axis label to name the varied quantity explicitly, e.g. 'peak-shaped load duration at fixed 40 rps peak (requests/month = 40 × peak-duration)', and add a one-line note that the canonical 6.24M marker is 156,000 s of peak load inside the 624,000 s active window.

issue: The figure's headline object — the frozen self-host line at $155,816.93/mo — is not visibly drawn in the plot area, and the legend's single pink swatch is keyed to two different encodings ('price band $15–25/K' and 'self-host $155,816.93/mo (21 hosts)'). As rendered, the plot contains only the blue cloud level, the red managed-price band, one green diamond, two vertical dotted lines and the hatched infeasible region. The reader therefore cannot see the crossing the caption asserts, cannot locate the 7.5M break-even, and cannot locate the 6.2–10.4M sensitivity endpoints. This is the figure's entire argument.
evidence: Caption: 'the frozen 21-host self-host line ($155,816.93/mo, case (i)/KV-screen sensitivity line, not an implied feasibility) crosses the managed API ...'. Legend entry 1: one pink filled swatch with two text lines 'price band $15–25/K' / 'self-host $155,816.93/mo (21 hosts)'. In the 150 dpi render no horizontal rule is visible at log10(155,816.93) = 5.19 (between the 1e5 and 1e6 gridlines); the only horizontal rule in the plot is the blue cloud level at ~8.76e4.
acceptance_test: Render PDF p. 278 at 300 dpi and confirm whether a horizontal self-host rule exists at $155,816.93/mo. If absent, add it in a distinct color/hatch with its own legend key and mark the three crossings (6.23M, 7.49M, 10.39M) on the x-axis. If present, split the merged legend entry into two keyed entries (band = filled swatch; self-host = horizontal line) and confirm the line is distinguishable from the band in grayscale.

issue: The price unit 'K' is never disambiguated anywhere in the figure: legend 'managed $20.80/K' and 'price band $15–25/K'; note 'a $15–25/1K price band'; y-axis 'Cost/month (USD, log)' against x-axis 'Requests/month (log)'. The book's own arithmetic requires $0.0208 per request, i.e. $20.80 per 1,000 REQUESTS: 155,816.93 / 0.0208 = 7,491,198.56 req/mo, and 6.24M × 0.0208 = $129,792/mo. Under the universal API-pricing reading ($/1K tokens) with the book's canonical 9,200-token request, managed cost per request would be 9.2 × $20.80 = $191.36 and the break-even would be 155,816.93 / 191.36 = 814 req/mo — a factor of ~9,200 away from the plotted 7.5M. A reader who reads '$/K' as '$/1K tokens' will invert the chapter's conclusion. (Escalates to P0 if Ch 16 does not define the unit explicitly elsewhere.)
evidence: Legend 'managed $20.80/K'; note 'sensitivity = a $15–25/1K price band moves the break-even to 6.2–10.4M req/mo'; printed p. 256 'the canonical 6.24M volume ($155,816.93/mo vs $129,792/mo — the ~7.5M API break-even sits above the canonical volume)'; 6,240,000 × 0.0208 = 129,792.
acceptance_test: Label the price unit explicitly in the legend and note (e.g. 'managed $20.80 per 1,000 requests'), and add one line to the note giving the per-request price ($0.0208) and the tokens-per-request assumption behind it. Verify against Ch 16's definition of the managed-API price unit; if Ch 16 defines '$/K' as per-1K tokens, recompute every number in the figure.

issue: The caption sentence appears to read 'crosses the managed API at the canonical 6.24M req/mo self-host sits above it' — placing the crossing AT 6.24M — while the figure's own annotation says 'break-even ≈ 7.5M' and the prose on printed p. 256 says 'the ~7.5M API break-even sits above the canonical volume'. evidence: Caption (PDF 278): '... crosses the managed API at the canonical 6.24M req/mo self-host sits above it.'; in-figure annotation 'break-even ≈ 7.5M'; printed p. 256 'the ~7.5M API break-even sits above the canonical volume'.
acceptance_test: In the source, confirm the caption reads 'crosses the managed API above the canonical 6.24M req/mo (break-even ≈ 7.5M); self-host sits above it'. If it reads 'at', correct it. Re-render and confirm the caption's number matches the in-figure 'break-even ≈ 7.5M' label.

evidence: Caption (PDF 278): 'Geometry: source log-log movement; 70B FP16 ≈ H100, 5-year amortization, $0.80/K API, fixed 21-host fleet'; legend 'managed $20.80/K'; note 'a $15–25/1K price band'.
acceptance_test: Check the source string; the caption must carry the same price as the legend ($20.80/K, with the unit disambiguated per FIG16-02). Re-render and confirm.

issue: The figure asserts a sensitivity REGION ('sensitivity = 6.2–10.4M req/mo (a region, not a point)') but does not encode it: no shading, bracket or pair of markers identifies the 6.23M and 10.39M band-edge crossings, and the vertical dotted line at ~7.5M carries no direct label or leader — its label sits in a red box in the upper-left, roughly two decades away in x.
